title: Refine project signed nonce and prefetch headers for streaming tools and OpenAI-compat
author: Maya Lin
description: Motivation: Streaming endpoints (SSE/WebSocket) + tool/function-calling flows require a short-lived, per-session nonce that can be validated both by the gateway and by the runtime worker. We saw two classes of flakiness in production: 1) browser preflight/CORS dropped custom signed headers during streaming handoffs; 2) scoped project tokens used in cookies or Authorization: Bearer were inconsistently mapped to the internal project/org headers, which broke worker-side authorization in mixed-hosting deployments. This PR introduces a small, backward-compatible surface that: (a) standardizes an X-Redwood-Prefetch header to carry a compact prefetched signature & metadata blob used during preflight and initial streaming handshakes; (b) introduces X-Redwood-Signed-Prefix to record which prefix of the request body was included in the signature (helps KV cache/keyed-signature stability for tool calls); (c) normalizes OpenAI-compat translation so Authorization: Bearer scoped-tokens are atomically mapped to X-Redwood-Project / X-Redwood-Org and a short-lived session nonce header (X-Redwood-Session-Nonce) when the compatibility layer is enabled. Backwards compatibility notes: the compatibility translation is opt-in via the existing openai_compat flag on the gateway; when disabled, behavior is unchanged. Checklist: - [x] implement header parsing and validation in gateway - [x] add runtime validation hooks for signed prefix and session nonce - [x] add CORS preflight whitelist for Redwood-prefetch and Redwood-session headers - [x] update openai-compat translation unit tests - [x] add e2e streaming test that exercises tool/function calling with prefetched nonce - [x] docs and upgrade note for self-hosted operators Description of change: 1) Gateway: new small parser for the X-Redwood-Prefetch header (compact base64 urlsafe JSON with fields: alg, ts, signature, meta). If present on OPTIONS or the initial streaming handshake, gateway validates the signature against the project key and attaches X-Redwood-Session-Nonce and X-Redwood-Signed-Prefix to the proxied request to workers. 2) Runtime: added a permissive nonce validator that accepts either a session nonce (short-lived) or fallback to signed-prefix verification on the first token exchange. This reduces spurious rejections when a worker sees a delayed KV cache entry. 3) OpenAI-compat: when openai_compat is enabled we now atomically translate Authorization tokens that match the scoped-token pattern (proj_{...}) into X-Redwood-Project / X-Redwood-Org headers and set X-Redwood-Session-Nonce to the derived session id. This avoids multiple round-trips for tool/function-calling flows that previously re-authenticated inside the runtime. 4) CORS: added Access-Control-Allow-Headers entries for X-Redwood-Prefetch, X-Redwood-Session-Nonce, X-Redwood-Signed-Prefix and updated the allowed methods for streaming handshakes. 5) SDK/Docs: added a short note in the OpenAI-compat migration guide and an example in the TS SDK showing how to include the Prefetch header from a browser client. Rollout plan: feature gated behind openai_compat + runtime flag 'accept_prefetch_nonce' for 2 weeks in canary, then enabled by default on dedicated hosts. Monitoring: new alert for "session-nonce-verification-failures" and graphing of prefetch header acceptance rate. Testing: unit coverage added for header parser, e2e test that spins up a canary worker + gateway and runs a streaming tool call with simulated preflight. Why unique: the prefetch abstraction explicitly separates the short-lived handshake artifact (prefetch signature) from the longer-lived Authorization mapping, allowing low-latency validation in the gateway without forcing the runtime to reparse or reverify large signed payloads.

review_comments: Priya Shah: Left a small comment on prefeth.go: we should clamp timestamp skew to 30s to reduce replay windows. Also, add a test for expired prefetch header.
Maya Lin (author): Addressed - added skew clamp and new unit test (tests/prefetch_expiry_test.go).
Darren Kim: Approve after nit - prefer header name X-Redwood-Session-Nonce over X-Session-Nonce for clarity. Good job keeping compat opt-in.

Noah Patel: Question on CORS behavior - will browser clients be able to send the prefetch header from a fetch() POST that becomes an SSE upgrade? Answer: we add the header to allowed preflight headers and ensure the initial handshake includes it; clarified in handler_streaming.go comments.
Security Team (automated): note - ensure HSM-backed signing keys used for project tokens; added to release checklist.

release_notes: Gateway: new X-Redwood-Prefetch header to carry prefetched signatures for streaming handshakes.
Compatibility: openai_compat now maps scoped Authorization tokens into X-Redwood-Project and X-Redwood-Org with an attached session nonce to reduce re-auth during tool/function calls.
Runtime: added permissive nonce validation path to reduce false positives during streaming tool handoffs.
Ops: new alert 'session-nonce-verification-failures' and rollout instructions in docs/openai-compat-migration.md
security_implications: No public breaking changes. Gate the feature behind openai_compat for hosted deployments. Recommend operators rotate project signing keys if they enable canary. Uses existing signing scheme; HSM/KMS recommended for production keys.
notes_for_operators: To enable: set gateway flag openai_compat=true and runtime flag accept_prefetch_nonce=true. Watch the new metric gateway.prefetch.accept_rate and alert if verification failures exceed 0.5% during canary.
